title: Coredns fails connecting to kube-api via kubernetes service
body: I upgraded my bare-metal kubeadm cluster to Kubernetes v1.28.1 on Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS with Cilium 1.14.1 and containerd 1.6.22. CoreDNS remains 0/1 because connections to the Kubernetes service at https://10.96.0.1:443 time out. The Cilium connectivity test also times out looking up kubernetes.default, although kubectl can reach the API server from outside the cluster and cilium status reports the components as OK. I suspect a regression after the upgrade.

symptoms_visible: Both CoreDNS pods remain 0/1 and log an i/o timeout connecting to https://10.96.0.1:443/version.
The Cilium connectivity test times out waiting for kubernetes.default to resolve, while kubectl access from outside the cluster works.
N0.label: N0 Kubernetes service connectivity failure reported

symptoms_visible: After forcing all nodes back to Kubernetes 1.27.5 and rebooting them, both CoreDNS pods are 1/1 Running.
N1.label: N1 compatibility downgrade restores CoreDNS

symptoms_visible: After upgrading all four nodes back to Kubernetes 1.28.1, the Cilium and CoreDNS pods are initially Running and ready.
N2.label: N2 controlled 1.28.1 reproduction before reboot

symptoms_visible: CoreDNS is healthy immediately after the upgrade, but after rebooting the cluster nodes it returns to 0/1 and times out connecting to the Kubernetes service.
N3.label: N3 failure reproduced by node reboot

symptoms_visible: CoreDNS remains 0/1 after the reboot and still cannot connect to the Kubernetes service IP.
N4.label: N4 cgroup attachment evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After upgrading every node to Kubernetes 1.28.2, the CoreDNS pods are still 0/1 and cannot reach the Kubernetes service.
N5_x.label: N5_x patched Kubernetes installed without reboot

symptoms_visible: New CoreDNS pods created after deleting the old ones are also 0/1 and still cannot reach the Kubernetes service.
N6_x.label: N6_x CoreDNS pod recreation aftermath

symptoms_visible: After rebooting the cluster on Kubernetes 1.28.2, both CoreDNS pods are 1/1 Running and all 42 Cilium connectivity tests complete successfully.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter-verified resolution

question_patterns: Did CoreDNS work on Kubernetes 1.28 before Cilium was upgraded, and which Cilium version did you upgrade from?
Can you tell whether the failure began with the Kubernetes upgrade or the Cilium upgrade?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not sure. I was using something older before the Kubernetes upgrade, then upgraded Cilium after the nodes were on 1.28. I don't know whether CoreDNS worked in between or which Cilium version I upgraded from.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: CoreDNS worked reliably on Kubernetes 1.28 until I upgraded only Cilium, and downgrading only Cilium restores it.

solution.intent: Test the supported compatibility baseline by returning the cluster to Kubernetes 1.27.5 while retaining Cilium 1.14.1.
solution.concrete_example: Downgrade kubeadm, kubelet and kubectl to 1.27.5, apply the downgrade on each node, reboot, and check whether CoreDNS becomes ready.

edges.comment: Reporter c1-c3 and c6: participant1 corrected the requested baseline to Cilium 1.14 on Kubernetes 1.27. The reporter forced Kubernetes back to 1.27.5 and observed both CoreDNS pods ready, but could not reconstruct the exact prior Cilium version or whether DNS worked between the two original upgrades.

solution.intent: Reproduce the transition under controlled conditions by upgrading the working cluster from Kubernetes 1.27.5 to 1.28.1 and observing it before reboot.
solution.concrete_example: Starting from the working 1.27.5 cluster with kube-proxy replacement enabled, upgrade every node to 1.28.1 and check Cilium and CoreDNS before restarting the nodes.

edges.comment: Reporter c12-c14: after restoring a working Cilium 1.14.1 configuration with kubeProxyReplacement=true, the reporter upgraded all nodes to Kubernetes 1.28.1. Cilium and CoreDNS remained healthy immediately after the upgrade.

solution.intent: Restart the upgraded nodes to test whether the failure depends on cluster boot ordering rather than package installation alone.
solution.concrete_example: Reboot all cluster nodes after confirming that CoreDNS is healthy on 1.28.1, then inspect CoreDNS readiness and API-service connectivity.

edges.comment: Reporter c14: the reporter rebooted all four nodes after the apparently successful 1.28.1 upgrade, and the CoreDNS readiness and Kubernetes-service timeout immediately resurfaced.

question_patterns: For a failing CoreDNS process, can you paste its /proc PID cgroup path and the corresponding bpftool cgroup tree output?
Please show the cgroup path containing CoreDNS and what BPF programs bpftool lists there.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For the failing CoreDNS process, `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` reports `0::/kubepods.slice/kubepods-burstable.slice/.../cri-containerd-43d307d27e57ee95b7b05eaec4ff4aba66f49df09ba9db4c6bcbfb71adc6e066.scope`. The matching `bpftool cgroup tree` entry only prints `453 device multi`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The CoreDNS process is under the expected cgroup hierarchy, and bpftool lists all the Cilium socket connect, bind, sendmsg, recvmsg and getpeername programs on its applicable ancestor.
The generated pod and container identifiers differ, but the matching entry still lists only the device program.

question_patterns: What filesystem type is mounted at /sys/fs/cgroup on each node?
Can you confirm whether these nodes use cgroup v1 or cgroup v2?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: All four nodes return `cgroup2fs` for `/sys/fs/cgroup`, and `mount` shows a cgroup2 filesystem mounted there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The nodes use cgroup v1 only; there is no cgroup2 filesystem mounted.

question_patterns: What cgroup root does the Cilium ConfigMap report, and does that path exist consistently on the nodes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Cilium ConfigMap says `cgroup-root: /run/cilium/cgroupv2`. That path looks populated on one control-plane node, but `ls` reports it missing on the other nodes.

edges.comment: Reporter c22 and c28, prompted by participant5 and participant7: these are the reporter's raw cgroup, mount and bpftool outputs. The conclusion that Cilium's socket-LB programs were attached under the wrong cgroup hierarchy is engineer-side and is introduced on the consuming solution edge.

solution.intent: Upgrade Kubernetes to 1.28.2 because the 1.28.1 startup regression can let the Cilium agent start before mount-cgroup and attach socket-LB programs to the wrong cgroup hierarchy.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade all nodes from Kubernetes 1.28.1 to 1.28.2, which contains the relevant startup-order correction, then re-establish the cluster boot state before validating CoreDNS.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers combined the reporter's cgroup output with their reproducer and packet tracing: the Kubernetes startup regression could start the Cilium agent before its mount-cgroup init container, leaving cgroup-v2 socket-LB programs attached at an ineffective hierarchy. That diagnosis was not stated by the reporter. Installing the patched packages alone was incomplete on the already-running cluster and did not restore DNS until the cluster was rebooted.

edges.comment: Participant5 c16-c18 and participant7 c24 supplied the accepted diagnosis; reporter c29 installed Kubernetes 1.28.2. The upgrade alone left CoreDNS unready, so treating package installation by itself as the complete remediation is a real falsified move.

solution.intent: Recreate only the CoreDNS pods after the Kubernetes patch upgrade to see whether fresh application pods recover service connectivity.
solution.concrete_example: Delete the existing kube-dns-labelled pods and allow the deployment to create fresh CoreDNS pods.

edges.comment: Reporter c29: deleting the old CoreDNS pods after upgrading created new pods, but both replacements remained 0/1. Pod recreation does not repair the node-level cgroup attachment state.

solution.intent: Reboot every node after installing Kubernetes 1.28.2 so Cilium initializes under the corrected container ordering, then verify CoreDNS and Kubernetes service connectivity.
solution.concrete_example: With Kubernetes 1.28.2 installed on every node, reboot the cluster, wait for the control plane and Cilium to initialize, then confirm CoreDNS is 1/1 and rerun `cilium connectivity test`.

edges.comment: Reporter c29: after upgrading to Kubernetes 1.28.2, neither waiting nor replacing CoreDNS pods helped. Rebooting the cluster then made both CoreDNS pods ready, and the reporter's Cilium connectivity run passed all 42 tests.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause for the reporter's chain: Kubernetes 1.28.1 could start the Cilium agent before the mount-cgroup init container, so with cgroup v2 and kube-proxy replacement the socket-LB BPF programs were attached at the wrong cgroup hierarchy and pod connections to the Kubernetes service IP were not translated.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the reboot-dependent reproduction and the collected cgroup evidence, including that the failing CoreDNS cgroup path did not show the Cilium socket programs.

The remediation must include upgrading every node to Kubernetes 1.28.2 or another patch containing the ordering correction and then rebooting the cluster so the corrected startup sequence actually runs.
Must not claim that installing the patched Kubernetes packages alone or merely deleting the CoreDNS pods resolves the existing broken node state; both were tried and CoreDNS remained 0/1.
Must ask the reporter to verify CoreDNS readiness and Kubernetes-service connectivity, such as by rerunning the Cilium connectivity test, before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes homelab or test-cluster operator who is comfortable with kubeadm upgrades and downgrades, Helm values, cluster-wide shell commands, bpftool, cgroup paths, and detailed reproduction steps.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, cooperative, and methodical; pastes command output, corrects ambiguous instructions, openly states uncertainty, and prefers understanding and reproducing the cause over resetting the cluster.
